# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

**Iteration 4/5. Parent = cand_0001 (val 0.975, 39 pass / 1 fail).** Two consecutive rejects
precede me (cand_0002 −0.100, cand_0003 −0.050), both branched off the same parent, and both
reported the *same* broke set overlap. That coincidence is the whole story of this iteration:
I spent the diagnosis budget on **why two structurally unrelated diffs broke the same three
tasks**, found a single shared mechanism, and built this candidate around it.

**No environment fault found.** I re-checked all 40 of this iteration's trajectories for infra
signatures before diagnosing anything as a capability gap: zero permission errors, zero
gateway/timeout/rate-limit errors, zero missing-binary errors, no truncated context, and no
traceback that was not the agent's own code. The one failing task (43436) is a genuine
capability failure. Nothing outside `prompt.md` and `task_template.md` was modified, and I ran
no command that mutates the adapter, harness, scorer, benchmark or environment.

## The central finding: the two prior rejects share ONE root cause, and it is not either diff

`LEDGER` records cand_0002 `broke={402-43, 560-12, 59595, 9569}` and cand_0003
`broke={402-43, 59595, 9569}` — an identical core of three, from diffs with no text in common
(cand_0002 edited verification procedure; cand_0003 added a date-interval domain rule). A rule
about counting open rows cannot break a percentile task, a "n/a" task and a header-copy task.
So the diff was not the cause on cand_0003; **latitude already present in the parent prose
was**, and both candidates merely re-rolled the dice on it.

I recovered the mechanism from the rejected candidates' own rollouts
(`.capevolve/run_suite/rollouts/val/<task>__<cand>__t0.json`), which is the highest-information
artifact in the run and neither RUNMAP nor INSTRUCTIONS points at it:

- **9569** — the failing agent wrote
  `earliest = round(float(v), 4)  # matches provided example: 0.170687841 -> 0.1707`.
  Init `AO9 = 0.1707` is the **only** non-blank cell in the 1280-cell graded range, and it
  **disagrees with gold** (`0.170687841`). The agent treated it as ground truth and rounded a
  correct answer to reproduce it.
- **59595** — the failing agent wrote the literal string `"n/a"` into C4:C6 to "preserve the
  workbook's demonstrated convention". Gold C4:C6 = `4, 6, 12` (ints). The trace shows it had
  **already printed the correct 4/6/12** and then discarded them. C7:C11's prefills *do* agree
  with gold, which is what made the mixed evidence convincing.
- **402-43** — cand_0003 copied the demo block `Sheet1!16:25` verbatim instead of building from
  the real source table; that block's header row lacks E/F/G labels, so E1/F1/G1 came out blank
  where gold expects `Col5/Col6/Col7`. cand_0001 built from the real header (row 1) and passed.

One sentence covers all three: **the agent treats a pre-filled value INSIDE `answer_position`
as a calibration target and reshapes a correctly-computed answer to reproduce it.** And in both
failing runs the mandated verify round *reported success* — because it re-derived with the same
wrong rule. Circular verification does not detect the error but does license changing values.

**Scaled to the class (the REAL test, measured over the whole verified-400):** of 379
single-range tasks, **268 (70%) have an in-range pre-fill**, and **148 (39% of all tasks; 55%
of the prefilled ones) have a pre-fill that DISAGREES with gold.** On val: 11 of 40 tasks
(267-18, 142-12, 382-10, 416-15, 48620, 6698, 9569, 9726, 55049, 59595, 56563). So this is not
a two-task quirk; it is the single largest latent-variance source in the parent prose, and the
parent's only defence is the soft phrase "weaker evidence … use it as a hint only".

## Ranked issue list (clusters, biggest leverage first)
| rank | cluster | tasks | shared root cause | tag | planned change class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | **P — in-range pre-fill treated as ground truth** | mechanism proven on 9569, 59595, 402-43 (the two rejects' shared broke set); class covers **148/379** tasks whose in-range prefill disagrees with gold, 11 of them on val | the parent calls a prefill "weaker evidence … a hint only" — a *strength* hedge, which leaves the agent free to adopt it when it has nothing else. It is not a hint at all: it is 55% likely to be wrong. No rule names the three concrete corruptions (display shadow, legacy placeholder, stale error) or forbids the three reshapings (round-to-its-precision, swap in its string, copy the demo block) | DECISION / KNOWLEDGE — a *variance* fix, not a val-point fix | STRUCTURE: replace the strength hedge with an explicit contract + the reason (why prefills are wrong) + a carve-out for EXTEND/CONSOLIDATE |
| 2 | **V — circular verification** | both failing runs on 9569 and 59595 printed "Mismatch count: 0" while holding wrong values | step 7 says "compare the printout against the answer you computed" without saying that recomputing by the same method is a tautology. So the verify round's only *actionable* output becomes "my value differs from the prefill" → it changes the value | BEHAVIORAL | STRUCTURE: state what the round is **not** for, and re-aim it at artifact faults only |
| 3 | **T — pre-rounding a float** | 9569 (proven); class = any task where the agent sees a rounded display shadow | the comparator rounds both sides to 2dp, so full precision can never lose — but the agent doesn't know that and rounds "to match" | KNOWLEDGE | CONTRACT: state the dominance argument, in both files |
| 4 | **D — open-at-a-date interval** | 43436 (the only remaining val failure) | instruction prose literally describes a mixed-instant test; gold's `COUNTIFS` uses `EOMONTH` on **both** bounds | KNOWLEDGE (domain definition, not derivable) | re-ship cand_0003's rule with a widened carve-out |

## Changes made this iteration (5 edits, 4 improvement types, both files)
| # | cluster | edit class (from guidance/system-prompt) | file | what & why it generalizes | protects passing? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | P | **ADD A SOURCED RULE + ADD THE REASON** (replaces a strength hedge with a contract) | `prompt.md` step 3 | "A pre-filled value inside `answer_position` is never a target to reproduce", followed by *why* (the three real corruption modes: display shadow, legacy placeholder, stale error) and the three forbidden reshapings. Closes with an explicit EXTEND/CONSOLIDATE carve-out. Stated over a class; no task id, cell, or answer appears | YES — BOUNDED. See blast radius below: audited task-by-task against 80-42, 463-17, 48588, 382-10, 416-15, 38462 |
| 2 | D | **ADD AN OMITTED RULE + WORKED EXAMPLE** | `prompt.md` §Getting the computation right | re-ships cand_0003's E1 (single-instant open-row count) with the gate folded into the bold headline and the carve-out widened to name "a 'last 7 days' total" | YES — BOUNDED, scope-audited: fires on 43436 alone among val tasks |
| 3 | V | **RESTRUCTURE (state what the step is NOT for)** | `prompt.md` step 7 | names the two failure modes of the verify round — it is not a re-derivation, and it is not licence to match a prefill — and re-aims it at *artifact* faults (unintended `None`, wrong type, unwritten cell, out-of-range write) | YES — BOUNDED. Strictly narrows what the round may *change*; every artifact check the parent had is retained verbatim above it |
| 4 | P | **RESTRUCTURE + TIGHTEN THE CONTRACT** | `task_template.md` step 2 | rewrites "Calibrate." so the *headline itself* carries the gate ("only against evidence from OUTSIDE `answer_position`"), and adds the instruction-wins tiebreak + "if no outside evidence exists, calibrate against nothing" | YES — BOUNDED, same audit as #1 |
| 5 | T | **TIGHTEN THE OUTPUT CONTRACT** | `task_template.md` §Output contract | "store full precision, round only when the instruction asks you to", with the 2dp dominance argument inline | YES — BOUNDED. 38462 is the one val task whose instruction demands rounding, and the carve-out names exactly that condition |

Improvement types applied: *add a sourced rule*, *add the reason*, *add a worked example*,
*restructure*, *tighten the output contract*, *soften/replace over-strong-or-too-weak wording*
(the "weaker evidence" hedge). Five edits across two files.

## Verify-the-fix — one line per edit, measured
Every line is a real run of the official
`third_party/spreadsheetbench/evaluation/evaluation.py` comparator against the real gold files
in `spreadsheetbench_verified_400`, or a direct read of the named rollout.

- **#1 REAL, at class scale** → swept all 379 single-range verified-400 tasks through
  `compare_cell_value` against gold: **268 have an in-range prefill; 148 of those disagree with
  gold.** 11 are on val. A rule that stops the agent reproducing a disagreeing prefill is
  therefore live on 39% of the benchmark, not on two tasks.
- **#1 mechanism, 9569** → failing rollout line: `earliest = round(float(v), 4)  # matches
  provided example: 0.170687841 -> 0.1707`. Init AO9 = `0.1707`; gold = `0.170687841`. Measured
  through the real comparator: **9** cells actually fail (all-or-nothing ⇒ reward 0). *Correction
  to an earlier subagent figure of "1261 of 1280": that was raw equality, not the scorer's
  `transform_value`, which rounds to 2dp. The true count is 9; the conclusion is unchanged.*
- **#1 mechanism, 59595** → failing rollout wrote `"n/a"` into C4:C6; gold = `4, 6, 12` (int).
  The same trace had already printed 4/6/12. Prefill C7:C11 *agrees* with gold, C4:C6 does not —
  a mixed prefill, which is why the "demonstrated convention" reading was persuasive.
- **#1 mechanism, 402-43** → cand_0003's rollout copied `Sheet1!16:25` verbatim; that block's
  header row has no E/F/G labels, so E1/F1/G1 → blank vs gold `Col5/Col6/Col7`. cand_0001 built
  from row 1 and passed. **Diagnosed as high-variance/incidental for cand_0003, not caused by its
  diff** (its diff was a date-interval rule with no bearing on header copying).
- **#3 / #5 dominance proof** → 200,000 random trials through the real comparator: storing **full
  precision → 0 failures**; storing the same value **pre-rounded to 4dp → 988 failures (0.49%)**.
  Two mechanisms: pre-rounding can cross the 2dp boundary (gold `0.145021572` → `0.15`, but
  `0.145` → `0.14`), and `round(-8.83e-07, 4) == -0.0`, which openpyxl round-trips as **int `0`**,
  breaking the `type(v1) == type(v2)` check. The rule is provably dominant, not a preference.
- **#2 (43436)** → re-read the real gold: its formula is
  `COUNTIFS(..., "<="&EOMONTH(...), ..., ">"&EOMONTH(...))` — EOMONTH on **both** bounds. The
  mixed-instant reading (which the instruction prose literally describes) mismatches 4 of the 5
  dept rows; `start <= T and (end is None or end > T)` matches **15/15 cells**. Robust to
  strictness: `end > T` and `end >= T` both pass.
- **#3 (step-7 anti-circularity)** → verified against both failing runs' own output: each printed
  "Mismatch count: 0" while holding wrong values, because the check re-ran the same rule. The
  edit removes the only actionable signal that check produced (value ≠ prefill) and replaces it
  with artifact checks, which are non-circular by construction.
- **Placeholder contract** → the adapter's own validator: `_task_template_error(dir) → None`;
  all six required placeholders present; `{max_turns}` present; **zero** unknown placeholders;
  a full `.format(...)` render with dummy values succeeds (5,158 chars). `_read_task_template`
  4,796 chars, `_read_system_prompt` 14,223 chars.

## Blast radius — per edit, named tasks and class
- **#1 / #4 (in-range prefill), BOUNDED.** The risk is the inverse case: 16 val tasks have
  prefills that *agree* with gold, and two are EXTEND/CONSOLIDATE tasks where the existing rows
  ARE part of the answer — **80-42** (47,975 agreeing in-range prefills; consolidate into "the
  first available blank rows") and **463-17** (17; the list "has been started"). Those drove the
  explicit final paragraph: *"Where the task is to EXTEND or CONSOLIDATE data that is already
  partly present, rows your method does not recompute simply stay as they are."* **48588** is the
  sharpest case — its instruction says "as I have manually done in Column B" and B2:B43 *is* the
  graded range; I read its passing trace and it **recomputes all 42 cells from scratch** and
  coincidentally reproduces the 17 prefills, which is exactly the behaviour the new rule
  prescribes. **382-10** (clears non-"comments" cells to `None`) and **416-15** (ISO strings →
  datetimes) already overwrite their in-range prefills with computed values. The parent's
  "re-writing a cell with the value it already holds is harmless" line is left in place above,
  so recomputing-and-agreeing stays explicitly licensed.
- **#5 (full precision), BOUNDED.** **38462** is the only val task whose instruction demands
  rounding ("round up … to the nearest whole hour"); the rule's condition — "round only when the
  *instruction* asks you to" — names that case. I also checked gold float precision per task:
  only 9569's gold carries >4dp, and no val task's gold is a deliberately-rounded shadow.
- **#2 (open-row count), BOUNDED.** Scope-audited across all 40 val tasks: 43436 is the only
  point-in-time open/closed-interval count. **59595** is the only rolling-window task, and it is
  correct *because* it uses two different instants — so the carve-out names "a 'last 7 days'
  total" explicitly, and (per cand_0003's lesson) the gate lives in the **bold headline**, not in
  a following sentence.
- **#3 (verify round), BOUNDED.** It only removes permission to change values; it adds no new
  action. Every artifact check from the parent's checklist is retained verbatim.

## Deliberately skipped
- **More edits for their own sake.** At 39/40 the reachable val gain is one task (+0.025) while
  the gate's resolvable effect is 2·SE ≈ 0.096 (~4 tasks) and any regression is instantly fatal.
  I shipped only edits with a measured mechanism; I did not manufacture riders.
- **Anything aimed at raising val directly beyond 43436.** There is nothing else failing. Edits
  #1/#3/#4/#5 are **variance reduction**: they target the latitude that made two prior
  candidates lose tasks they should have kept. Expected val effect is neutral-to-positive on
  val and positive on held-out test, where 39% of tasks carry a disagreeing prefill.
- **Re-litigating cand_0002's verification prose.** `rejected.jsonl` shows it added
  corroborate-your-interpretation procedure; this candidate does the structural *opposite*
  (it removes interpretive latitude from the verify round), so it is not a re-proposal.
- **Any per-task literal.** No task id, sheet name, cell reference, date or expected answer
  appears in either file. The example numbers in the prose (`0.1707`, `"n/a"`, `#NUM!`) are
  illustrations of a corruption *class*, and `0.145021572` is a synthetic 2dp-boundary
  demonstration, not any task's answer.
- **Prose workarounds for infra.** No environment fault exists to work around.

## Process & features used
- **Subagents:** read-only background agents, no writes, no worktrees, no workflows. One to
  recover the shared mechanism from the two rejects' rollouts; one to sweep the verified-400 for
  the prefill-disagreement statistic; one scoped **only** to the passing tasks ("find instructions
  that would make a passing agent behave differently"); and a final **adversarial review of my own
  draft** — the process rule cand_0003's META_INSIGHTS recorded, which has now caught bugs in my
  draft two iterations running.
- **Order of operations, corrected from cand_0003's lesson:** mine the rejected batch's
  *mechanism* → gate the draft against passing tasks → only then verify efficacy. cand_0003
  verified efficacy first and wasted the work when the edit turned out unsafe.
- **Ground truth:** every claim re-run through the official comparator on real gold files.
  `/tmp` traces were read via `python3 -c "print(open(...).read())"` (the Read tool lacks `/tmp`
  permission in this session).
- **Prior iterations read:** `prior_iterations/cand_0001`, `cand_0002`, `cand_0003` (PROCESS.md +
  diff.patch), plus `LEDGER.md`, `JOURNAL.md`, `INSIGHTS.md`, `META_INSIGHTS.md`, `RUNMAP.md`, and
  `.capevolve/run_suite/rejected.jsonl`.

## Good things to PRESERVE
- Everything cand_0001's PROCESS.md lists (literal-value contract, `data_only=True`, non-writing
  verify round, non-quota checklist, blank's two meanings, date-component carve-out).
- **The EXTEND/CONSOLIDATE carve-out at the end of step 3.** Without it, edit #1 is a live threat
  to 80-42 and 463-17.
- **"Round only when the *instruction* asks you to."** Removing that clause breaks 38462.
- **The gate inside the bold headline** of the open-row rule. cand_0003 measured that an
  ungated headline breaks 15 of 16 cells on 59595.
- **Step 7 must not invite re-derivation.** That is the mechanism by which two candidates
  reported "0 mismatches" on wrong answers.
